sections.title: 4. Eligibility to Study Mechanical Engineering PG in Ireland

items: Generally, applicants will need a recognized bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or closely related engineering discipline.
Some common eligibility requirements include:
- Undergraduate degree - BE, BTech or equivalent
Engineering background relevant.
Academic performance to the required level for honors classification or equivalent of university.
Bachelor education in mathematics, mechanics, thermodynamics, materials or related engineering subjects.
English language proficiency, as needed
Indian students' eligibility
“Indian applicants are generally assessed on the basis of their bachelor’s degree, CGPA or percentage, university recognition, duration of the course and subject matter.
The most direct route is a BE or BTech in Mechanical Engineering.
Applicants from Automobile, Aerospace, Manufacturing or Mechatronics Engineering may also be considered, subject to the program.

sections.title: 5. Admission Requirements for Mechanical Engineering PG in Ireland

items: Education Requirements
Typically, universities will ask for:
Bachelor’s Degree Certificate or Provisional Certificate.
Official transcripts of your academic record.
Information on overall marks, CGPA and grading system.
Information on relevant courses/projects if asked.
Proof of relevant work experience, if applicable
English language requirements
International students may need to submit IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic or an equivalent qualification.

The standard benchmark for many postgraduate programs is an IELTS score of around 6.5 overall, with varying minimum and individual scores, depending on the institution and course. You might be exempt from certain rules.
Other Requirements
Applicants may also be required to (varies by programme):
Purpose statement.
References of academic or professional nature.
Curriculum Vitae (CV) or résumé.
Information on research, design projects or internships.
Research proposal for a research degree.
Application fee payment.

sections.title: 6. Cost of Doing Mechanical Engineering PG in Ireland

faqs.q: 1\. What are the universities for Postgraduate Mechanical Engineering in Ireland?
faqs.a: 8\. Mechanical Engineering Recognition and Accreditation in Ireland If you want to move toward professional engineering recognition then accreditation is important. In Ireland, Engineers Ireland accredits appropriate engineering programs to professional education standards. Accreditation is dependent on the specific qualification and program, and a postgraduate master's is not automatically accredited just because it is offered by a recognized university. Before you apply * Check the accreditation status of the specific course and award. * See which graduation years are represented. * Check whether your undergraduate qualification also satisfies the academic requirements for the professional pathway you wish to pursue. Know the difference between a *MSc, a ME / MEng and an accredited professional engineering qualification. * Check for any other recognition requirements in the country you want to work. 9\. Salary and Job Scope after Mechanical Engineering PG in Ireland Mechanical Engineering graduates may work in design, manufacturing, energy, product development, automation, transport and research. Career opportunities depend on technical skills, experience, employer needs and market demand. Potential roles in the workplace * Mechanical Design Engineer * Manufacturing Engineer * Project Engineer * Quality Engineer * Robotics and Automation Engineer * Energy Engineer * Materials Engineer * Research and Development Engineer * Maintenance or Reliability Engineer Indicative gross salary ranges per year Entry level / Graduate Engineer Positions \| €32,000 - €42,000 Experienced Engineers \| €42,000 - €65,000 Senior / Specialist Engineers \| €65k-€85k+ Indicative planning estimates only, not official salary bands or guaranteed outcomes. The actual salaries depend on the sector, the employer, the location, the technical specialization and the experience. 10\. Documents Required for PG in Mechanical Engineering in Ireland The specific checklist differs by university but common requests are for: * Passport valid. * Certificate of Bachelor’s degree or provisional certificate. * Official transcripts of all semesters/years. * Explanation of grading scale or CGPA if requested. * English-language test results, if required. * An up-to-date CV or résumé. * Purpose statement or personal statement * Academic or work references. Information about relevant *projects, internships or work experience. * Research proposal for research-based programs, where applicable. * Receipt of payment of the application fee, if applicable. * Certified translations of documents not issued in an accepted language. Proof of financial means and health insurance* for immigration purposes where required. 11\. FAQs about PG in Mechanical Engineering in Ireland Mechanical Engineering: ME, MSc - University of Galway Trinity College Dublin - Master’s Pathway in Mechanical Engineering , Also worth checking DCU and UCD for related postgraduate engineering programs and specializations.

faqs.q: 2\. What is the duration of Masters in Mechanical Engineering in Ireland?
faqs.a: Taught master's programs are often one year full-time. Check the official course page for details. Some course structures, such as research degrees and others, may take longer

faqs.q: 3\. Can a BTech student of Automobile or Mechatronics Engineering apply?
faqs.a: Perhaps. Some universities accept related engineering disciplines but this depends on the subject prerequisites for the course and your academic background. Please confirm with the admissions team that you are eligible before applying.

faqs.q: 4\. What is the cost of PG Mechanical Engineering in Ireland?
faqs.a: 2026/27: University of Galway charges €28,640 for its MSc and ME Mechanical Engineering programs and Trinity College Dublin charges €27,780 for its Mechanical Engineering / Zero-Carbon Technology master's. Fees subject to change, living expenses are extra.
